question: Which part of closed-system evolution is a physical assumption, and how does a differentiable unitary curve determine a Hermitian generator?
entry: Exact3.1 pure-state postulates and2.6 Hermitian exponentials/derivatives; matrix product rule and time/energy units stated locally.
exit: Adopt unitary evolution; derive H=i*hbar*dotU*Udagger and its Hermiticity, state equation and constant-H solution; explain endpoint nonuniqueness and time-dependent limits.
assumptions: Differentiable finite-dimensional complex-linear unitary U(t), with fixed reference time U(0)=I
Closed-system evolution is adopted as a physical postulate, not derived from a single-state norm test
Hamiltonian=i*hbar*dotU*Udagger; constant Hamiltonian only for exponential solution
Declared reference time t0 and dimensionless tau=t/t0,K=t0*Hamiltonian/hbar in code; no calibrated device model

symbols.U,dotU: Evolution from reference zero and its entrywise time derivative
symbols.Hamiltonian,hbar: Calligraphic H denotes Hamiltonian in energy units; hbar is the reduced Planck constant
symbols.tau,K: Dimensionless time and specified constant matrix in the worked example
symbols.c,I: Real scalar energy shift and identity
